slides.title: Online Multimodal Workload Assessment in Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a transparent framework for assessing interaction workload in contact-rich pHRI using interaction wrench, kinematics, and skin conductance. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: An interpretable multimodal framework for online interaction workload assessment in contact-rich physical human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Integrates interaction wrench, TCP kinematics, and skin conductance into four interpretable factors, using path curvature and task progression for context-adaptive weighting.
card.evaluation: Evaluated with 24 participants across 18 environmental conditions; used leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation against pupil diameter and learning-based baselines (MLP, TCN, LSTM).
card.limitation: Correspondence with the physiological reference is weak near task onset (ρ_early = 0.002).

slides.title: ForceDelta-VLA: Distilling Force-Conditioned ActionCorrections for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: ForceDelta-VLA introduces a distillation framework that separates reference actions from force-based corrections, improving success rates and reducing peak contact forces in contact-rich manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: ForceDelta-VLA improves contact-rich manipulation by distilling force and delay corrections to a reusable reference action.
card.key_idea: A lightweight policy distills explicit correction targets from a frozen teacher's paired force-conditioned and force-agnostic predictions, using asynchronous schedule replay to handle reference-action delays.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on nine real-robot tasks; achieved 82.2% mean success (vs 54.4% ForceVLA) and reduced mean peak contact force by ~26%.
card.limitation: Fails when connectors jam or contact is lost, as corrections cannot always trigger necessary retreats or approach changes.

slides.title: XRoboToolKit-T: Teleoperation with High Stability and Precision with Tactile Sensing for Contact-rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a teleoperation system using a tactile-informed force control architecture to improve stability and precision in contact-rich tasks. It utilizes haptic modules and a vision-language-action model to refine manipulation actions based on real-time tactile sensing.

card.one_liner: XRoboToolKit-T is a tactile-driven teleoperation system enhancing stability and precision for contact-rich robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines a real-time stabilizer estimating pseudo shear forces to suppress aggressive movements with a VLA-based refiner for high-level corrective action adjustments based on tactile images.
card.evaluation: Tested on syringe insertion and pipette tasks using UR5 arms. Outperformed Twist2 in grasping efficiency (138 vs 128 successful manipulations/15min).

slides.title: TAO-Force: Unifying Force-Aware Perception and Fast-Slow Control for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: FORCE-CONDITIONED VLA FRAMEWORK FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: TAO-Force integrates force-aware perception via F-FiLM and a fast-slow control architecture to enable compliant, responsive robotic interaction in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: TAO-Force integrates force-aware perception and fast-slow control to improve contact-rich robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Uses F-FiLM to modulate frozen VLA representations with force feedback and a contact-gated architecture switching between slow position-control and fast admittance-control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-world tasks using AgiBot G1; achieved 80.0% ID and 64.2% OOD average success rates, outperforming GR00T N1.7 and π 0.5.
card.limitation: Success rates drop under OOD conditions when tool geometry changes, affecting contact timing and force characteristics.

slides.title: TacBPM: A Tactile-conditioned Behavior Prior Model for Dexterous Reorientation
slides.tldr: TACTILE-CONDITIONED BEHAVIOR PRIOR FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tactile-conditioned behavior prior model that distills multi-scale sphere specialists into a latent controller to improve stability and training speed for dexterous reorientation.

card.one_liner: TacBPM uses a tactile-conditioned behavior prior to accelerate and stabilize dexterous in-hand object reorientation.
card.key_idea: Distills multi-scale sphere specialists into a variational latent controller; downstream policies learn residual latent actions while keeping the tactile-proprioceptive prior frozen and adapting the decoder.
card.evaluation: Tested on anisotropic objects, commanded-axis rotation, and arm-hand tasks using PPO. Outperformed raw-action baselines in success rates and sim-to-real transfer.
card.limitation: Performance gaps remain when extrapolating to very large object scales or specific novel shapes from the frozen sphere-trained prior.

slides.title: SWIM: Vision-Language-Grounded Soft Whole-Body Interactive Manipulation
slides.tldr: VLA FRAMEWORK FOR SOFT ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: SWIM introduces a vision-language-action policy for soft robots that maps instructions and RGB observations to actuation sequences, contributing to RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: SWIM enables language-grounded soft robot manipulation via virtual-rollout command sequences and geometric supervision.
card.key_idea: A VLA policy combining a diffusion action head with Visual Soft Proprioception (VSP) for geometric body-anchor supervision, deployed via virtual rollouts to avoid online latency.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on packing, reaching, and grasping using a planar tendon-driven robot. Simulation success reached 100%/96%/88%; physical success reached 100%/80%/75%. Results outperform OpenVLA-OFT baseline.
card.limitation: Limited to planar manipulation, predefined reset configurations, and anchored grasping targets.

slides.title: UniDex-ViTac: Learning Unified Visuo-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation Policy from Human Video Data
slides.highlight: UniDex-ViTac leverages human-video-guided simulation to train a dexterous manipulation policy that integrates point clouds and fingertip contact signals, improving success rates on both seen and unseen objects.

card.one_liner: UniDex-ViTac learns a visuo-tactile dexterous manipulation policy using human videos and simulation-generated contact data.
card.key_idea: Residual RL specialists adapt human video references into robot demonstrations with tactile signals, which then train a single ACT-based generalist using point clouds and binary contact tokens.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 10 YCB objects in simulation and 11 physical trials (seen/unseen). Achieved 66.4% real-world success, outperforming the point-cloud-only baseline by 11.8%.
card.limitation: Uses sparse binary contact signals, discarding force magnitude and detailed location, and exhibits sim-to-real discrepancies in tactile sensing regions.

slides.title: ProxiDex: Learning Dynamics-Guided Proximity Policy for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: DYNAMICS-GUIDED PROXIMITY POLICY FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: ProxiDex introduces a hardware-agnostic contact representation using hand-object proximity to stabilize dexterous manipulation under visual occlusion and contact uncertainty.

card.one_liner: ProxiDex improves dexterous manipulation by modeling hand-object proximity dynamics to handle visual occlusions and contact uncertainty.
card.key_idea: A framework using reconstructed interaction point clouds to learn action-conditioned forward-inverse latent dynamics, which adaptively reweights proximity cues and guides policy inference via dynamics-consistency.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Adroit, DexArt, and real-world tabletop tasks against baselines like CordViP; showed higher success rates (83.9% sim, 72.6% real) and better occlusion robustness.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate object reconstruction/tracking and suffers from accumulated prediction errors during prolonged occlusions; cannot measure real contact forces.
